1) Aggrieved by the impugned Decree and Award, dated 26.03.2012, passed in M.V.O.P. No. 617 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Kadapa,
whereby, the claim of Rs.5,40,440/- was awarded to the Claimants towards compensation,

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Kadapa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: M.A.C.M.A. No. 985 of 2014 is filed by the Claimants for claiming remaining balance compensation amount and M.A.C.M.A. 1013 of 2015 is filed by the sole respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C., questioning the legal validity of the Award passed by the Tribunal.

Since, both these appeals are filed against one Award and Decree, dated 26.03.2012, passed by the Tribunal in M.V.O.P. No. 617 of 2008, both these appeals are heard together and disposed of by way of Common Judgment.
2) For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the Appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3) The claim petitioners filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [the 'M.V. Act'], and Rule 455 of A.P. Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 [the 'Rules'] read with Act 54/1994 against the respondent claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the death of one T.Ramachandra Reddy [the 'deceased'], in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 04.09.2008.
4) Facts germane to dispose of the Appeal may briefly be stated as follows: -
i. On 04.09.2008, the deceased boarded the bus of A.P.S.R.T.C. bearing registration No.AP11 Z 4787 to proceed to Nandalur.

At about 5.30 P.M., when the bus reached Neetipalli Bridge, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus and due to application of brakes suddenly, the deceased was thrown out from the bus and sustained multiple and grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries.

A case in crime No. 62 of 2008 was registered against the driver and conductor of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C.
5)

The sole respondent filed counter with a plea that the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the deceased.

1 6) Based on the above pleadings, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
(i) Whether the deceased T. Rama Chandra Reddy S/o. Narasimha Reddy died owing to rash and negligent driving of the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing N. AP11 Z 4787 owned by Respondent?
(ii) Whether Respondent is liable for the compensation claimed by the petitioners?
( iii )
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed by the petitioners?
(iv) To what relief?
7) During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioners, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A5 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent, no witnesses were examined and no documents are marked.
8) At the culmination of the enquiry and on appreciation of the entire evidence available on record, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.5,40,440/- towards total compensation to the claimants.
Aggrieved thereby, the claimants and the sole respondent preferred the aforesaid appeals separately.

9) Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
10) Now, the point for determination is:
i) Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?

If so, to what extent?
ii) Whether the appellants/claimants are entitled to remaining balance compensation amount, as prayed in the claim application?

11) POINT Nos. (i) & (ii): The case of the claimants is that, on 04.09.2008 the deceased boarded the bus of A.P.S.R.T.C. bearing registration No.AP11 Z 4787 to proceed to Nandalur, and when the bus reached Neetipalli Bridge, at about 5.30 P.M., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus and due to application of brakes suddenly, the deceased was thrown out from the bus and sustained multiple and grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries.

A case in crime No. 62 of 2008 was registered against the driver and conductor of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C.
12)

In order to prove rash and negligent driving of the driver of the A.P.S.R.T.C.
offending bus, the petitioners relied on the evidence of PW1 to PW3.
PW1 is not an eye witness to the incident.

PW2 is the Conductor, who traveled in the offending bus Thotli Venkata Padmavathi Another vs Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92988676/
2 by the time of incident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The evidence of PW2 goes to show that the driver of the offending bus drove the offending bus in a rash and negligent manner and there is no negligence on the part of the deceased.

On considering Ex.A1 - certified copy of the F.I.R., Ex.A4 - certified copy of the charge-sheet and on considering the entire material on record, the Tribunal arrived at a conclusion that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.AP11 Z 4787, in which the deceased sustained severe injuries and died at the spot itself.
The Tribunal also came to the same conclusion.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.
13) The case of the claimants is that, the deceased was aged about 49 years and he was working as 'driver' in A.P. State Road Transport Corporation and his gross salary was Rs.12,193/- per month.
In order to prove the same, the petitioners filed salary certificate of the deceased, which was marked as Ex.A5.

On considering the material evidence on record and on considering the documentary evidence, I am of the considered view that the gross salary of the deceased was Rs.12,913/- per month and after deducting statutory deduction i.e., provident fund and profession tax [Rs.1,274/- + Rs.100/- from out of Rs.12,913/-] an amount of Rs.11,539/- is available to the dependents of the deceased.
Since, the deceased was aged about 49 years, the relevant multiplier applicable for the age group of deceased as per the decision of Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1 is "13".

entities.text: Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, the dependents are two in number, 1/3rd amount has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
In total Rs.18,00,084/- [Rs.11,539/- x 12 x 13] is the total income, out of which 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.12,00,056/- [Rs.18,00,084/- - Rs.6,00,028/-] is awarded to the claimants towards 'loss of dependency'.
The Tribunal committed a grave error by taking the net salary drawn by the deceased, which is Rs.3,738/-.
The same is not justifiable.
The statutory deductions are only to be deducted out of the gross salary of the deceased.
The Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' to the 1st petitioner and an amount of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of estate and love & affection'.
In total, the claimants are entitled to an amount of Rs.12,30,056/-.

In the result, the appeal filed by the A.P. State Road Transport Corporation vide M.A.C.M.A. No.
1013 of 2015 is dismissed and the appeal filed by the claimants vide M.A.C.M.A. No. 985 of 2014 is partly allowed.
The claim of Rs.5,40,440/- awarded by Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.12,30,056/-.
The claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.6,89,616/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till the date of realization.

The respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C. is directed to deposit the said enhanced compensation of Rs.6,89,616/- with interest at 6% per annum,
as ordered above, within two months from the date of this judgment.
On such deposit, the claimants are entitled to withdraw the same along with interest therein equally.
No order as to costs.
